Whether a change to an applied row has been approved

seal_approved.Rd

Three conditions, and none is enough on its own.

Usage

seal_approved(register, events, creators, approvers = character())

Arguments

register

The register as read, one row per request.

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

creators

Who created each row, as log_creators() answers, in the order of register. "" approves nothing.

approvers

The IT accounts whose approval counts on any row, as REDCap usernames.

Value

A logical vector, one answer per row.

Details

The approval has to carry this row's seal. A value that is some other seal approves some other version of the row, and accepting it would make one approval stand for every change that came after it.

It has to come from whoever created the row. Not merely from somebody other than the author of the change: the request is the creator's, the scope gate checks the creator's rights on the project every round and nobody else's, so an approval from a third referent would grant on the word of somebody whose rights on that project nobody has looked at. The seal detects that the row moved; only the log can say who approved it and who created the row, because it names whoever was authenticated rather than a value somebody typed – which is the same reason requested_by cannot be trusted alone.

And it has to be newer than what it approves: above the round's last execution and above every change somebody other than the creator made, as log_approval_stands() reads the log. The value alone cannot say so. approved_seal is never blanked, so an approval the round has already carried out would approve again any later change that brings the row back to it; and the seal is a public hash of the intent fields, so it can be pasted before the change it names exists.

IT approves as the creator does, decided on 2026-10-15: the accounts named in approvers stand where the creator stands, under the same three conditions. It is what keeps a request whose creator has left UBEP from waiting for ever, without deleting the row and losing who filed it. The list lives on the machine that runs the round and never in this repository. One limit is worth knowing: the scope gate still asks the creator's rights on the project, so no approval, from IT or anybody else, carries a row whose creator no longer manages the project.

An unreadable log is not this function's to decide. It answers about the events and the creators it was handed, and a caller holding neither gets FALSE on every changed row: the row waits, which is the direction that does not grant.
